review_scope: Viewed four matching temporal samples (frames0,27,54,80) from existing native128/R1-400/R6-128 videos. These are selected diagnostic examples, not a new aggregate metric or continuous-motion verification.

records.visible_observation: All begin with separated blue liquid-like beads. R1 retains a comparatively narrow bead column and small splash; R6 shows larger changing splash structures in the middle/end samples, also present to some degree in native128. The sampled images do not clearly show several intact balloons rising and then simultaneously bursting.
records.implication: The requested event is not established by PC5. More prominent splash structures accompany the R6 SA increase but do not establish correct requested sequencing or improved physics.

records.visible_observation: The first image contains four rounded objects on a flat surface. In the R6 middle/end samples a green object has a markedly thicker, cupped/elongated appearance and a broad dark interior/underside, while the sampled R1 green object preserves a more clearly bounded disk form. These sparse views cannot separate every perspective effect from deformation or establish exact impact continuity.
records.implication: R6 is not simply different in color or motion amount: visible shape consistency is a relevant issue alongside its PC regression. No clear tethered poi swing and soft-surface impact is established in these sampled views for any model.

use: Evaluation-only observations. Do not use as training targets or claim a new validated physics score.
